P1.evidence: The application was consulted only to check the spelling of his name — 'I saw something different in the application, so I just want to check' — so nothing substantive was read back. The frame covered two of four parts: 'go over where you're at the moment, where you want to go, see if we can help you bridge that gap.' Agreement obtained ('Sounds good? Yeah. Perfect.'). Open question asked verbatim.

P2.evidence: The most complete baseline in the batch. Age asked directly. Work asked and the two-job, two-night-shift pattern established: 'what sort of work do you do?' P2d was the best injury probe anywhere in this batch — a one-to-ten pain scale on the knee, a check for other injuries, and a specific follow-up on the back, hips and legs after spotting a gesture. Training reality established ('for the last two, three weeks, I didn't do anything at all'). Nutrition asked and probed to cheat-meal frequency. Energy asked and linked to the night shifts. Sleep only surfaced inside the energy answer and was never asked directly, and health conditions were never asked.

P3.evidence: A one-to-ten on appearance, then 'where do you feel like that comes from the most?' The bridge ran properly: 'why is it important for you to actually get towards that sort of physique for yourself?' and the follow-up unpacked a vague answer — 'When it comes to confidence, do you mean like when you go to a beach or what do you mean with confidence?' The reflect-back was clean. Two gaps. P3f was never asked — no partner, family or colleague was ever brought in. And when he produced the deepest line in the batch — 'I want to see myself in the best physical shape I can get it before I die' — the rep's next words were 'Okay, how old are you actually at the moment?'

P4.evidence: The best Phase 4 in the batch. P4f ran in almost scripted form and worked: 'when you were saying that you didn't really have the time when it comes to working out consistently, is that really the case? Or was it more so a moment of priority back then?' produced 'maybe it was an excuse'. He then pressed again: 'would it have been impossible to just drop to the floor, do 100 push-ups a day and at least get that sort of consistency there?' — 'No, it wouldn't have been impossible.' He ran the same move a second time at the very end on nutrition. Past attempts were only volunteered rather than asked, which is the one weakness.

P5.evidence: P5a was asked properly: 'six months, a year from now, you're still at the exact same place, maybe lost a little bit of body fat. How would that be for you when that is the case?' The prospect deflected the whole premise — 'I don't think that this will happen. Because my body, I think I have a very good metabolism' — and the rep praised the deflection instead of pressing: 'I like that mentality. You're not even talking about what happens if it doesn't work out.' The consequence frame collapsed at exactly the moment it was needed, the same failure mode as the Brandon Blair call.

P6.evidence: Both commitment questions ran and both landed. 'Do you feel like if you have the structure for yourself, it is at home, Trevor is out to guide you with everything... that you're also going to stick to it? Or do you feel like when life gets busy, you're just going to throw it to the side again?' produced 'I'm certain I can stick to it', followed by an explicit promise. P6b ran again before the price. P6c falls short because the prospect had already flagged the constraint — 'I definitely do, but it depends also from the cost' — and the rep presented without testing capacity.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted after the refusal, and no payment link was sent even for the downsell — details were to follow on WhatsApp.

objection_plays.detail: Well isolated: 'outside of the investments, yeah, you feel like it is something you see yourself doing. You feel like, yeah, I want to commit to this. It's just the investments blocking it.' Capacity was asked and clarified as a total rather than monthly. The worth-it test ran and produced a clean value acceptance. But none of the six financial-picture moves ran — no cash on hand, no monthly leftover after bills, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments — and no plan was offered on the six-month price before the rep moved to a cheaper product.

The strongest OA execution in the batch. Trigger: 'I'll give you my answer by Monday.' The rep asked permission to challenge, tested urgency against the prospect's own stated need — 'you do feel like you have to take action for yourself as soon as possible. Is that correct?' — challenged the date twice, and extracted a promise: 'Can you promise yourself that you're going to go over it when you're not that busy, so on Saturday, and then on Saturday you're going to come back to me and we can get you started with it?' Scripted moves that did not run: 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now'.

notes: Phases 2, 3, 4 and 6 were all executed at the highest standard in this batch, and the call was still lost on the one thing that was never tested — capacity. The prospect had signalled it before the presentation ('I definitely do, but it depends also from the cost') and the ceiling turned out to be a sixth of the price. Second point, and it is a coaching point rather than a criticism: the two moments where he pushed back on a comfortable answer, the excuse question in Phase 4 and the Monday-to-Saturday challenge, are the best selling on the call. The corresponding failure is Phase 5, where the prospect deflected and was praised for it.
